You are worker W19 (ORCHESTRATION track O) in R&D round 3 for the Rust crate at C:\Users\mariu\neural-mesh. The director verifies by independent rerun. Honest ceiling: decomposition/verification/retrieval per step make multi-step research more reliable; no discovery or intelligence claims.
READ: results/g5_board_entry.md, src/research.rs, src/defaults.rs, src/knowledge.rs, src/bin/g5_study.rs (in-bin replica of run_task with a custom router), src/bin/e3_research.rs, f7_research.rs, results/research_board.md (E3/F7), and results/g9_board_entry.md if it exists (W10 is concurrently working critic/multistep on bins g9_*; do not touch those files, avoid duplicating: you own orchestration policy).
TASK: new bins src/bin/g18_*.rs (+src/bin/g18_common/), results/g18_*; you may NOT edit src/*.rs (proposals -> results/g18_proposed_patch.md). Build a multi-step research-task world: each task is a DAG/chain of 3-6 sub-steps; sub-steps have types (lookup, compute, synthesize, check) needing different specialists; later steps depend on earlier outputs (an early wrong step propagates); each step has graded quality, hidden per-agent per-type competence, recurring context for retrieval, and a verification check with imperfect recall; calls cost. Baseline: single-shot routing of the whole task to one agent. Then orchestrators: (1) decompose + route each sub-step by type; (2) + per-step retrieval; (3) + per-step verification and retry/reroute on failure (replan-on-failure); (4) learned stopping (stop verifying when confidence is high); (5) parallel fan-out of independent sub-steps. Metrics: end-to-end task quality (all-steps-correct rate and graded), call-cost, quality-per-cost, sample-efficiency. Compare vs best fair baseline from {keyword, eps-greedy, pooled-thompson, hebbian-robust, warm(hebr), guarded-safe} applied single-shot, and vs the previous orchestrator level. Controls: single-step tasks and tasks with independent steps where decomposition should not help; worlds where verification is expensive and errors rare (it must learn to skip). Protocol: tune seeds 1-8, held 31-60, confirm fresh 61-90, paired 95% t-CI, Holm, wins in >1 independent world generator; fix worlds before policies. Report which level actually moves quality and by how much.

No downloads/crates, no git commits, don't kill processes. HONESTY: measured only.

handback.t:
W19 (orchestration track O) is finished. Everything is a seeded simulation I wrote. It measures what decomposing, routing, retrieval, verification and learned stopping do to graded quality and cost in a world I defined. It says nothing about real LLMs or discovery.

**Files** (`src/*.rs` untouched, no commits). The main one is `results/g18_board_entry.md`, which holds the VERIFY REQUEST blocks (A–D), the negatives and the exact rerun commands.
- Code: `src/bin/g18_orch.rs`, `src/bin/g18_common/mod.rs`.
- Results in `results/`:
  - `g18_orch.{json,log}` (held 31-60)
  - `g18_orch_confirm61-90.{json,log}` (fresh seeds, same frozen tuning)
  - `g18_sens.{json,log}` and `g18_sens_confirm61-90.{json,log}` (sensitivity)
  - `g18_orch_run1_mu0.1_tuning.{json,log}` (first run, kept on purpose)
  - `g18_world_examples.txt`, `g18_check.log`, `g18_proposed_patch.md`

**Setup.** There are 15 worlds, fixed before any policy was run. Generator A is specialist pipelines (6 worlds), generator B is latent-factor agents with random DAGs (4 worlds), plus 5 controls. Each task has 3–6 dependent steps of four types, with hidden per-agent per-type competence, error propagation, recurring-project notes, a verifier with imperfect recall, and call costs.
- Baselines: 6 fair single-shot routers, plus `ss-warm+retr`, a single-shot router given the same notes as a control for the retrieval confound.
- Levels:
  - L1: decompose and route per step
  - L2: add retrieval
  - L3: add verify with retry/reroute
  - L4: add learned stopping
  - L5: add parallel fan-out
- Protocol: tuned on seeds 1-8, held 31-60, confirm 61-90, paired 95% t-CI, Holm per family.
- Determinism: two reruns of the 61-90 file are identical apart from `runtime_s`. Four unit tests pass.

**Which level moves quality** (graded H1500 vs the best fair single-shot, generator A | generator B; 61-90 matches within about .006):

| Level | Graded gain | Cost | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| L1 decompose + route | +.214 \| +.003 (ns) | unchanged | Real only when specialists differ by step type |
| L2 retrieval | +.080 \| +.067 more (all-correct +.275 \| +.103) | +.225/task | Largest generic lever; scales about linearly with the context-dependence parameter I set |
| L3 verify + retry/reroute | +.026 \| +.039 more (all-correct +.089 \| +.085) | +50% / +87% (pipe-main 4.73 → 6.97; lat-main 4.72 → 8.64) | Utility-negative once a unit of cost is worth more than about 0.05 quality; harmful with a noisy verifier |
| L4 learned stopping | quality ≈ L3 in A (+.001), −.008 in B | about 5.0 vs 7.0 in pipe-main | Checks per task drop from 5.19 to 0.63 |
| L5 parallel fan-out | 0 in all 15 worlds | none | Latency only: −0.33 in pipe-main, −2.1 in lat-main, −3.5 with independent steps |

- **Pure orchestration is smaller than it looks.** Against a single-shot router given the same notes, L2 gains +.29 in pipe-main but only +.02 in lat-main (other B worlds ns). L3 and L4 beat it Holm-significantly in 6/6 A and 4/4 B worlds.
- **Wins in both generators.** L2–L5 win against the best fair baseline in all 10 treatment worlds. L1 wins only in generator A.

**Controls and negatives**
- **L1 on a dominant agent:** L1 loses −.011 (Holm LOSS) in the dominant-agent, independent-step control. In the other controls it is ns, except the specialist, independent-step control (+.185).
- **Controls against baselines without notes:** L2–L5 "win" in every control against baselines that have no notes, because retrieval is the lever there, not decomposition.
- **Verification can hurt:**
  - In the poor-verifier world (`sig_v` .22), L3 is not better than L2 and all-correct drops −.065.
  - At `sig_v` .4, L3 is −.048 graded.
  - L4 is the best arm there.
- **Cheap, noisy verification:** part of L3's gain is best-of-k selection under agent noise, not error detection. In the equal-agents control L3 gains +.042 graded for +6.3 cost per task.
- **Rare errors, expensive checks:** L4 skips and cuts cost by 4.14 per task versus L3 with quality unchanged. At cv = 1.0 that skip is a prior rule, not learned. At cv .1/.3 it does learn, but still pays a small exploration tax versus no verification at all (utility −.002 to −.003).
- **Disclosure — tuning change:** my first run tuned L4 at utility weight mu = .1 and hit the never-verify grid edge. I changed only the L4 tuning utility (mu .03, wider grid), added metrics, and reran everything; worlds were untouched. Both runs are kept. The honest reading at mu = .1 is "don't verify at these prices".
- **Other limits:** the retrieval model is a stochastic stand-in, not the real index. No drift was tested for L4. Costs and parallelism are my own accounting.

**Proposals** (`results/g18_proposed_patch.md`): a step-level `run_plan` entry point, a `VerifyGate` for stopping, and a verifier/reroute contract. Of the library-level ideas, fan-out only justifies a scheduling helper.
